prompt: Your phone is worth $\$500$ new and loses $20\%$ of its value each year. How many dollars is it worth after 2 years?
hint: Each year the phone keeps part of its value. Find the percent it keeps and use that as a multiplier.

hints.text: Each year the phone keeps part of its value. Find the percent it keeps and use that as a multiplier.
Keeping $80\%$ means multiplying by $0.80$ each year. After one year the value is $500 \times 0.80 = 400$. Apply the factor once more.
$400 \times 0.80 = 320$, so the phone is worth $320$ dollars after $2$ years.

explanation: Losing $20\%$ a year means the phone keeps $80\%$ of its value, so the yearly factor is $0.80$.
Two years means applying the factor twice: $500 \times 0.80^2 = 500 \times 0.64$.
Multiplying gives $320$, so the phone is worth $320$ dollars after two years.

alternativeExplanations.title: Year-by-year table
steps: Notice it loses $100 the first year but only $80 the second — decay shrinks by a factor, not a fixed amount.

alternativeExplanations.title: Slice off a fifth twice
steps: Losing 20% = losing one fifth. One fifth of 500 is 100, leaving 400.
One fifth of 400 is 80, leaving 320. Value: $320.
